g1.want: tools/doororder.py finishes, and test_door_rows.py's slowest case stays under the 180s per-test timeout

g2.want: a checkout's components can be provisioned from any starting state without losing untracked build output or somebody's work

i1.what: one CallGraph scope evaluation costs time proportional to the sum of the value-set sizes it touches

i2.what: metta._atoms.model.encode's return slot holds 3,104 abstract references, and every frozenset union, difference and membership over it is linear in that size

i3.what: the order must be maintained while the graph is still being discovered

i4.what: verdicts become more conservative, so the generated _orders.py changes

i5.what: _external_call returns Reference('unknown', '<site>: external value <external name>'), so an unresolved member on an external value makes one distinct unknown PER EXTERNAL NAME PER SITE, and those flow into every set the value reaches

i6.what: the analysis still scales badly: 158 modules take 15.6s and 171 take 460.7s, thirty times the cost for eight per cent more program

i7.what: reset --mixed leaves the working tree, so a component whose tracked files git removed when the path became a gitlink stays missing them

i8.what: on the merged tree the analysis DEGRADES thirty-one doors: verdicts that were Verdict(1), Verdict(2) or a clean dependency all become the same Verdict(None, mixed, open, recursive, dependency)

i9.what: _attribute returns Reference('unknown', f'undeclared member {parameter}.{member}') for a member a supplied parameter does not declare, which is one abstract value per parameter TIMES member

a1.title: schedule scopes by a topological number maintained as call edges are discovered, instead of a FIFO deque

a2.title: process the worklist depth-first, popping the newest scope

a3.title: widen a value set past a threshold to one unknown reference

a4.title: intern each Reference to an integer and carry Values as an int bitmask, so union, difference and membership stop being linear in set size

a5.title: memoise the container item-slot union in _protocol's __iter__ expansion, through the class's existing _memo that evicts when a read slot grows

a6.title: memoise the same container item-slot union in _assign's destructuring branch, keyed by the element slot it reads

a7.title: keep memoising the pure recomputations the profile names, now _container_call and what remains of _protocol

a7.1.title: name the union one concept, _stored(container, slot), and have all three sites call it

a8.title: carry the SITE and not the external name in the unknown that _external_call returns

a9.title: check the tracked files back out after the reset, refusing only on a MODIFIED file and ignoring gitlinks, which are the nested components the recursion sets

a10.title: carry one canonical value for an undeclared-member read, leaving the parameter and member in open where they are read

a11.title: key the solve cache on the sources, entries and lifetimes it reads, instead of on the whole row set

a12.title: collapse the strongly connected components of the value-flow graph so the scopes in one cycle share a single set instead of each holding a converging copy

r37.says: read in _analysis.py and _order.py: _call adds to open per unknown reaching it, and derive builds its graph from bodies.get(target)

r39.says: committed; test_door_order.py passes whole, 123 tests. It does not make test_door_rows.py pass, because one solve is still 460s

r40.says: applied and under measurement: the door-order suite passes whole with it, 123 tests, and no test asserts the text it coarsens; its effect on the 12,527-entry open sets is being measured

c14.says: collapsing strongly connected components is the established fix for exactly this symptom, and it is precision-preserving: every pointer in an SCC of the constraint graph provably converges to the SAME set, so one representative can stand for all of them

r41.says: Fahndrich, Foster, Su and Aiken, PLDI 1998, measure that the bulk of work and execution time is attributable to SCCs and that without cycles the analysis scales very well; Hardekopf and Lin PLDI 2007 add lazy and hybrid cycle detection; Pearce, Kelly and Hankin SCAM 2003 give online detection by keeping the graph topologically sorted

r42.says: measured: the degraded doors sit on an SCC of 152 scopes in metta._atoms.factories, and the cost model is stored references times mean set size, which an SCC divides by its own size

c15.says: the two cycles in this analysis are different things and only one is a cost artefact: a cycle in the VALUE-FLOW graph means several slots provably converge to the same set, so collapsing it is representation and nothing else; a cycle in the CALL graph is what Order.cycles publishes as recursive=True and is a real property. Neither is a termination check, so collapsing the first cannot make the analysis miss a loop a developer wrote

r43.says: user, 2026-09-19: with SCC we don't prevent the dev to create an infinite while loop; and Order.cycles is read by Verdict as recursive

c16.says: collapsing the undeclared-member value DOES cut the open sets, against this thread's own earlier reasoning: 12,527 to 9,290 entries, 26 per cent, because those unknowns are CALLED elsewhere and each distinct one added its own open entry at each call site

r44.says: measured on the merged tree before and after
